note: Seed rules for the hackathon. Summaries are plain-English paraphrases, not legal text. Savya: fill every clause marked TODO from the official CCPA notification and keep summaries short.

CCPA2024.title: CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Greenwashing or Misleading Environmental Claims, 2024 (notified 15 Oct 2024)

PWM2024.title: Plastic Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2024, G.S.R. 201(E), 14 Mar 2024

CPCB_LIST.title: CPCB: List of certified manufacturers/sellers of compostable carry bags & commodities (as of 26.10.2023)

rules.name: Vague green terms need qualifiers and substantiation
rules.summary: Terms like eco-friendly, green, sustainable, natural, clean, pure, organic, cruelty-free, carbon-neutral, eco-conscious, good for the planet, minimal impact or regenerative may be used only with accurate, accessible qualifiers, substantiation and disclosures.

required_evidence.desc: Says which aspect (product, part, packaging, process, disposal) and how
Or verifiable evidence / a link or QR to details

rules.name: Specific environmental claims need credible certification or scientific evidence
rules.summary: Claims such as compostable, degradable, free-of, non-toxic, recyclable, renewable, climate-positive and net-zero need credible certification, reliable scientific evidence, or verifiable evidence from a statutory or independent third party.

required_evidence.desc: Named certifier or standard that covers this claim and this product

rules.name: Material details must be accessible (QR code or URL)
rules.summary: Detailed material information behind a claim should be disclosed through a QR code, URL or similar, be easy for consumers to access, and include unfavourable as well as favourable findings.

required_evidence.desc: A QR code or link to the details behind the claim

rules.name: The claim must state its scope
rules.summary: A claim must say whether it refers to the whole product or part of it, the manufacturing process, the packaging, use or disposal, or a service.

rules.name: Comparisons need data on what exactly is compared
rules.summary: Comparative claims must rest on verifiable, relevant data and say exactly what is being compared. 'Greener than the competition' alone is not enough; 'first' or 'only' claims are comparisons too.

required_evidence.desc: Data, method and baseline for the comparison

rules.name: Future promises need an actionable plan
rules.summary: Aspirational claims (for example 'net zero by 2030') may be made only with clear, actionable plans for how they will be achieved.

required_evidence.desc: Concrete plan, milestones or a linked roadmap

rules.name: Compostable plastic needs a CPCB certificate and IS/ISO 17088 conformity
rules.clause: Rule 4(1)(ha) (CPCB certificate before marketing or selling); Rule 4(1)(h) (IS/ISO 17088:2021)
rules.summary: Makers of compostable plastic carry bags and commodities must hold a CPCB certificate before marketing or selling, and compostable plastic must conform to IS/ISO 17088:2021.

required_evidence.desc: Maker found on CPCB's certified list

rules.contradiction_note: Compostable plastic is still plastic under these rules, so 'plastic-free' or '0% plastic' on a compostable plastic product conflicts with the definition.

rules.name: Compostable items must carry the industrial-composting label
rules.summary: Each compostable plastic item must bear the label 'compostable only under industrial composting'.

required_evidence.desc: Required label visible in text or photos

contradiction_signals: breaks down naturally in the environment
rules.contradiction_note: Compostable plastic must be labelled for industrial composting only, so saying it composts at home or breaks down naturally in the environment conflicts with the required label.

rules.name: Biodegradable plastic: no microplastics, a label with days and environment, and a CPCB certificate
rules.clause: Rule 3 definition of biodegradable plastics (as substituted); Rule 11(4); Rule 4(1)(ha)
rules.summary: Biodegradable plastic must degrade by biological processes without leaving microplastics or visible or toxic residue, must state the number of days and the environment in which it degrades, and its maker needs a CPCB certificate.

required_evidence.desc: CPCB certificate (the list we hold covers compostable makers; mark Needs review if not found)
Number of days and environment stated

rules.contradiction_note: A product described as breaking into fragments, or made of conventional polyethylene with an additive, doesn't fit the 2024 definition of biodegradable plastic.

rules.name: A certificate must cover this claim and this product
rules.summary: Certifications must come from credible statutory or independent bodies and be relevant to the claim. Company-level badges (B Corp), fragrance-safety certificates (IFRA) or natural-origin ingredient certificates do not back claims like eco-friendly, compostable or plastic-free.

required_evidence.desc: cert_scope is 'product' or 'material' and matches the claim

rules.name: Puffery and mission statements are not product claims
rules.summary: Obvious exaggeration that isn't misleading, generic colours or pictures that aren't misleading, and a company mission statement not tied to a specific product are outside the guidelines.

rules.name: Technical environmental terms must be explained in plain words
rules.summary: Technical terms such as Environmental Impact Assessment, greenhouse gas emissions or ecological footprint need consumer-friendly language that explains what they mean for this product.

required_evidence.desc: A plain-language explanation of the technical term and what it means for this product

rules.name: Nature slogans and imagery need real substance behind them
rules.summary: Words, symbols or imagery that suggest a product is environmentally responsible, such as 'gentle on nature', without relevant details or context are misleading.

required_evidence.desc: Specific details of the environmental benefit the slogan suggests

rules.name: Research results must be disclosed in full, not only the favourable parts
rules.summary: Data from research must not be selected to highlight only favourable observations while hiding unfavourable ones; claims citing studies or tests should give access to the full results.

required_evidence.desc: A link or QR code to the full study or test report, unfavourable results included
